reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes a Bitcoin-mining opportunity claiming that a $3,500 position produced roughly 11 Bitcoin and about 1.1 Bitcoin per month. It describes buying a share, recruiting participants into binary teams, maintaining monthly qualifications, and receiving percentage commissions, referral payouts, and daily dividends. The records do not verify that the mining, payments, or claimed returns occurred.

citations.quote: Master distributor of #BitClubNetwork Joe Abel presents the #Bitcoin mining opportunity in Tacoma WA August 2015.
what we're really doing is we're quote-unquote selling Bitcoin mining equipment and getting a commission on whatever Bitcoin mining equipment they buy
the more blocks we find the more bitcoin we get the more dividends get paid out. We get paid daily dividends
my 135 hundred main position has produced me Roughly 11 Bitcoin plus so ten point nine eight Bitcoin so one point one Bitcoin per month.
The 3,500 was my interest to run my business and the interest to run my business has made me $300,000 in ten months and with another 1.5 million dollars in equity buildup.

opening.argument: Judge, the presentation does not describe every payout as automatic. It distinguishes a participant's reported experience from the conditions for earning team compensation: the speaker says repurchase timing depends on how the account is set up, and the qualification slide says a member who misses the monthly requirement moves back to the rank they achieved. Those limits matter when assessing whether the presentation promises an unconditional return.

citations.quote: sometimes takes 2 days or a couple days, depending on how you have it set up

rebuttal.rebuttal: The cited Bitcoin output is explicitly the speaker's account of his own position, not a quoted guarantee that another buyer will receive the same amount. The opening also says the records do not verify mining or payments; lack of verification does not, by itself, establish that the account is false. The stated monthly qualification requirement further limits the claim that commissions simply accrue to everyone.

citations.quote: my 135 hundred main position has produced me Roughly 11 Bitcoin plus so ten point nine eight Bitcoin so one point one Bitcoin per month.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Conditions on team compensation do not neutralize the investment pitch. The presentation attributes substantial Bitcoin output to a purchased position, says mining produces daily dividends, and describes commissions tied to other people's purchases. A listener is still being encouraged to expect mining and recruitment income; the cited timing and rank conditions do not substantiate those returns.

you are gonna receive 12% of whatever they buy

opening.argument: Judge, this segment can be read as an explanation of how the proposed operation and compensation plan are supposed to work. The speaker breaks an illustrative $1,000 into equipment, operating costs, and affiliate compensation, then explains why equipment would be shipped to a shared mining location rather than installed by each buyer. The slides diagram team placement and rank requirements. Those are explanations of a model, not independent proof that its claimed payouts occurred.

citations.quote: lets say $1,000 comes into BitClub. $400 of that goes to buy the mining equipment
but they don't take delivery on it in California and North Carolina and setup in their basement and try mining Bitcoins.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening correctly identifies descriptions of shares, mining, and commissions, but those descriptions are also the subject of the presentation's operational explanation. Its example begins as a hypothetical allocation, not an audited account of where any particular buyer's payment went. That distinction supports reading the segment as a walkthrough of asserted mechanics rather than treating every diagram as verification of a payout.

citations.quote: So what is basically happening is lets say $1,000 comes into BitClub.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Explaining mechanics does not make the segment merely educational. The description calls it a Bitcoin mining opportunity, while the speaker connects the proposed equipment purchases to daily dividends and tells listeners that referral income is money they can use to pay bills. The diagrams serve that promotional account; they do not verify mining output or payments.

citations.quote: Master distributor of #BitClubNetwork Joe Abel presents the #Bitcoin mining opportunity in Tacoma WA August 2015.
the more blocks we find the more bitcoin we get the more dividends get paid out. We get paid daily dividends
this is real money that you can pay your bills tomorrow with.

opening.argument: Judge, the speaker describes a purchase of mining equipment coupled with an affiliate commission, and gives an allocation for a hypothetical $1,000 purchase: equipment, operating costs, and referral compensation. He also explains that buyers would not take delivery and run the equipment at home. This record does not establish whether the equipment was actually purchased or the mining took place, but that evidentiary gap should not turn a described commercial service into a proven sham. Assess what the presentation shows, while keeping its unverified claims separate from proof of fraud.

citations.quote: what we're really doing is we're quote-unquote selling Bitcoin mining equipment and getting a commission on whatever Bitcoin mining equipment they buy
$400 of that goes to buy the mining equipment that all gets shipped up to Iceland. $200 of that goes to pay the electric bill and run the company
but they don't take delivery on it in California and North Carolina and setup in their basement and try mining Bitcoins.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening points to buying shares and earning recruitment commissions, but the speaker expressly frames the purchase as funding equipment and its operation. It also concedes the record does not verify whether mining or payments occurred. That leaves the alleged failure of the underlying service unestablished, even though the sales claims warrant scrutiny.

citations.quote: $400 of that goes to buy the mining equipment that all gets shipped up to Iceland. $200 of that goes to pay the electric bill and run the company

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The equipment story is itself a sales claim, not evidence of delivery or operation. Buyers are told they will not take possession of the equipment, while the presentation promises daily mining dividends and commissions extending through recruits' purchases. The case does not require proof that a promised payment failed: the observable content is a promotion of paid mining returns intertwined with recruitment income.
